displayText: Two quick reminders. The gradient at a point is the slope of the tangent there, the line the secants settle onto as the second point slides in. And e to the x is its own derivative. On the graph, that means at every point, the gradient equals the height, the y value. Where the curve is one unit high, the tangent's slope is one. Where it's about two point seven high, the slope is about two point seven. Height and gradient always match, and that's our measuring stick.
